title: Chapter 2 — The Primary
description: A party ticket in your pocket is not a ticket on the ballot. The delegates have to "affirm" you, and so does Chief Lanre, who wanted it first.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The party primary. Ninety-one delegates in a hired hall with ceiling fans that only spin when somebody important walks under them.

beats.speaker: chiefLanre
beats.text: (a big man in a bigger cap, the other aspirant) Teacher! Welcome to politics. (He hugs you. His cologne hugs you separately.) The delegates are... expensive this year. Inflation. I hope your Baba is generous.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Delegates want "mobilisation". ₦1,000 each is an insult. ₦2,000 is a greeting. Lanre is paying ₦3,000. Your call.

options.text: Pay ₦2,000 each. It's how primaries work.
Ask Baba Oko to "handle" the delegates.
Give a speech instead. Make them ashamed to take Lanre's money.

perfect.toast: Two delegates give Lanre's envelopes back. On camera. The hall goes very quiet.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The count. Lanre's people count loudly. Your people count carefully. The returning officer counts whatever he is told to.

beats.speaker: chiefLanre
beats.text: (after the result, very friendly) Teacher, you won. Fine. But listen: step down for me, and when I am councillor, you will be Supervisor for Education. A car. An office. A driver. Think of your pension.

beats.speaker: chiefLanre
beats.text: He means it. He has done this deal before.

options.text: "No, Chief. The ward knows my face."
Step down. Take the Supervisor job.

beats.title: The Primary
beats.summary: The party has affirmed you, at a price. Chief Lanre is smiling at you from across the hall in a way that has nothing to do with happiness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You step down "in the interest of party unity". Chief Lanre wins the ward. The Supervisor job arrives eight months late, with a car that has no battery.

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: (at home, very calm) You gave away the ward for a car with no battery. (She laughs until she cries, then just cries.)

beats.title: Party Unity
beats.summary: You stepped aside for a promise. The promise kept you waiting, and then kept you quiet.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Independent candidates need five hundred signatures from registered voters in the ward. By Friday. Seyi has a clipboard and a theory: "People will sign anything if you hold the pen out confidently."

beats.objective: Collect signatures: start at the Front Stop.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Front Stop: a hundred and forty signatures, mostly from people waiting for the danfo who were bored.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Market: two hundred, after Mama Titi shouts "Sign for the Teacher, he wrote things in a notebook!" from her stall.

beats.speaker: babaTicket
beats.text: (at the motor park) Drivers sign for drivers' friends. Are you our friend, Teacher? A union office in the new market, maybe?

options.text: "If I win, the union gets a desk at every council meeting. Not an office. A voice."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Five hundred and twelve signatures. Seyi kisses the clipboard. "Independent and legal. Owó Ńlá will hate it."

beats.title: The Primary
beats.summary: No party, no godfather: just five hundred and twelve signatures and a clipboard Seyi now considers lucky.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: (grabbing your sleeve) Teacher. Listen to me. Lanre has made this deal four times. Four "Supervisors". One of them is still waiting for his car. You won the primary. Ninety-one people said your name.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Lanre is waiting with his hand out.

options.text: "Sorry, Chief. The ward knows my face."

beats.title: The Primary
beats.summary: The party has affirmed you, at a price. Chief Lanre is smiling at you from across the hall in a way that has nothing to do with happiness.
